summary.headline: GRP Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 60% to INR174 million, margin 11% (+233 bps), PAT more than doubled to INR42 million on 26% total income growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 26% YoY to INR1,573 million, driven by Pyrova Energy utilisation, export recovery and better realisations. EBITDA grew 60% to INR174 million with margin up 233 bps to 11% despite sharp raw material inflation. Management re-segmented into Rubber Recycling and Others, and for the first time gave a directional FY27 outlook of close to 20%+ revenue growth. Pyrova cleared a 25-day monthly continuous run threshold in July 2026, and the rCB plant is slated for commissioning by October 2026.

segments.name: Rubber Recycling (Reclaim Rubber, Custom Die Forms, Pyrova Energy)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue grew 34% on a stand-alone basis with reclaim volumes +12%; margins expanded on realisations and efficiencies. Pyrova is still below stand-alone profitability; cumulative Pyrova investment is about INR91 crore.

segments.name: Others (Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefin, Windmill, residual polymer composite)
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly flat against a higher base that included polymer composite, which was permanently shut after the tariff hit. Engineering plastics volumes +27%; plastic verticals EBITDA margin up 14 pp YoY on a 10-pp gross margin improvement.

guidance_outlook: FY27: close to 20%+ overall revenue growth, driven by Pyrova, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling.
FY27: reclaim rubber volumes to grow close to 20%; management hopes to hold double-digit volume growth for the year.
Reclaim rubber, mid-term: mid-teen volume growth over 3 years, double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin from ~9-10% toward 10-14% after Pyrova synergies.
Pyrova: capacity to 45,000 tons, then +30,000 tons in FY28; EBITDA margin to 18-20% after rCB is mature (later described as 15-20%); FY28 seen as maturity year.
Plastics: over 20% growth in FY27, mid-teen growth through FY30, EBITDA margin 10-15%. Management said current margin is not one-time and should keep improving.
FY27 capex INR90-100 crore; FY28 capex decision in 2H FY27. Remaining ~INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan still to be deployed.
capex_capacity: Pyrova: two more pyrolysis lines to take capacity to 45 KTA; longest continuous reactor run achieved; July 2026 met threshold of 25-day monthly run with 4-day shutdown.
rCB (recovered carbon black) plant: commissioning starts next month (August 2026), target commissioning by October 2026; meaningful contribution expected by Q4 FY27.
Reclaim rubber debottlenecking capex included in FY27 plan.
Long-term: another 30,000 t pyrolysis and 12,000 t rCB capacity in Gujarat; Pyrova stand-alone revenue potential INR250-300 crore.
Renewable energy was ~48% of stand-alone power in FY26 (37% a year earlier); target 50% by FY28, expected to be reached in the current fiscal.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth ~30% YoY vs volume +12%; the balance is price, largely passed through to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually.
Management does not expect rubber prices to reverse soon; cited El Nino effects on natural rubber and oil-linked synthetic rubber pricing.
Reclaim is being pitched as a value alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches.
US exports recovered (export volumes +20%, mostly North America); Europe and other markets starting to contribute. Non-US indirect tariff-related volumes not fully recovered.
Domestic reclaim market share up ~1% YoY per management; export share flat overall but higher in focus geographies.
Engineering plastics growth driven mainly by automotive OE demand, with early appliance approvals contributing; polyolefin volumes flat as customer selection tightened.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin moderated on higher raw material costs (management cited ~180 bps decline)
More than doubled; after prior period items

qa_highlights.question: Has the tariff disruption led to permanent changes in the competitive landscape, and did GRP win customers from global competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer composite was permanently shut, a real one-time loss. Reclaim and Custom Die Forms volumes are back to pre-tariff levels, with currency adding a margin benefit versus pre-February 2026. Some customers are starting to receive tariff credits, which may lift margins later, but visibility is limited. Indirect non-US export volumes are not fully recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Which business will be the largest contributor to earnings growth for the rest of FY27, and does management expect double-digit revenue growth and further margin expansion in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated close to 20%+ revenue growth for FY27, driven by Pyrova Energy, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling. It said the Q1 margin is not one-time and should keep improving, but it did not give a separate gross margin number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rCB project status, including customer trials, expected revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pyrolysis phase was commissioned in October 2025 and stabilised by March 2026. The rCB plant starts commissioning in August 2026 and is targeted for October 2026. Meaningful contribution is expected from Q4 FY27. Pyrova can reach 18-20% EBITDA margin once rCB is mature, subject to customer approvals; FY28 is seen as the maturity year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 27% growth in engineering plastics volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly automotive OE demand for nylon, with early appliance approvals from Q4 FY26 contributing some commercial volume. Polyolefin revenue grew but volumes were flat because customer selection was tightened, with a push into specialty polyolefin sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How much has rubber inflation risen over the past year, and when will prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict how long rubber inflation will last. Revenue grew about 30% against 12% volume growth, so the balance is price, largely passed to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually. Prices are not expected to reverse soon given El Nino and oil-linked synthetic rubber.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 capex plans, and what is the deleveraging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR90-100 crore, covering two more pyrolysis lines to reach 45 KTA, the rCB plant and reclaim debottlenecking. FY28 capex will be decided in 2H FY27. About INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan remains. Deleveraging timing is not in management's control, and there are no firm plans, though it would be needed to accelerate the Gujarat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers shifting toward sustainability-led material solutions rather than buying on price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a combination of value and sustainability. Reclaim is increasingly considered an alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches. In plastics, regulation drives conversion and cost drives adoption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery is demand normalisation versus share gains, and is the export order book back to pre-tariff levels? What is the sustainable EBITDA margin, and when does Pyrova become EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose 20%, mostly North America, with early Europe contribution. Domestic market share is up about 1% YoY, and export share is flat overall but higher in focus geographies. Pyrova crossed a 25-day monthly continuous run with a 4-day shutdown in July 2026. Management did not give a date for EBITDA breakeven. Stand-alone EBITDA margin targets are Reclaim 10-14%, Pyrova 15-20% and plastics 12-15%.

risks_watch: Rubber and raw material inflation: gross margin fell about 180 bps and management would not guide on gross margin; pass-through lags 1-4 quarters under quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts.

Pyrova execution: still below stand-alone profitability, with margins in single digits during ramp-up. rCB commissioning targeted October 2026, but several quarters may be needed for tire-industry product approval.
Indirect non-US export volumes not yet recovered; polymer composite closure is a permanent revenue and margin loss.
Capex and leverage: FY27 capex of INR90-100 crore, FY28 capex decision deferred to 2H FY27, and no firm deleveraging plan.
Plastics: polyolefin volumes flat on tighter customer selection; nylon growth depends on automotive demand; EPR enforcement and waste collection remain challenges.
Possible tariff credits to customers could affect margins, with timing and size not yet visible.
key_quotes: The threshold in the industry from a performance perspective is for a run of minimum of 25 days in a month and a 4 -day shutdown on the pyrolysis.
I do believe that this margin that we have generated in Q1 is not a onetime margin generation.
So, I wouldn't want to comment on the gross margin number.
At least as things stand now, we do expect these businesses to start generating cash flow.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the integrated platform, Pyrova milestones and the first-ever FY27 outlook, but cautious on near-term pricing, rCB timing and FY28 capex. Management declined to forecast rubber price direction or gross margin and framed several targets as conditional on customer approvals.
